name: Command & Control Frameworks
tagline: C2 / post-exploitation frameworks, implants, and tunnel helpers — for authorized adversary simulation, C2-traffic detection testing, and lab post-exploitation.

tools.name: Sliver
tools.desc: Open-source cross-platform adversary-emulation framework (BishopFox); Go implants are dynamically compiled with per-binary encryption keys and support C2 over mTLS, WireGuard, HTTP(S), and DNS.
tools.when: Your default lab/red-team C2 when you want a framework blue teams can profile exhaustively without commercial licensing.

tools.name: Havoc
tools.desc: Modern malleable post-exploitation framework pairing a Qt client with a Go teamserver; the Demon agent speaks AES-encrypted HTTP(S)/SMB and uses indirect syscalls. Maintenance stopped — repo archived Feb 2026 — yet it stays a heavily studied, MITRE-tracked (S1229) traffic class.
tools.when: Lab and detection research against a well-documented post-exploitation stack (tunnel, AMSI/ETW patching, BOF/COFF loading) whose artifacts most EDRs now fingerprint.

tools.name: Mythic
tools.desc: Collaborative, Docker-based post-exploitation platform whose core ships no agents; you install agent payload types (Apollo/.NET, Athena/Rust, and others) and C2 profiles as separate containers via mythic-cli and the Mythic scripting API.
tools.when: Long-running lab engagements needing a pluggable, community-vetted agent ecosystem, cross-team collaboration, and GraphQL/automation hooks for red-team reporting.

tools.name: Merlin
tools.desc: Go-based post-exploitation server/agent pair communicating over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, h2c, and HTTP/3 (QUIC) — a practical model for non-TLS and modern protocol beaconing.
tools.when: Lab tests of HTTP/2 and QUIC transport detection, since most defensive tuning focuses on plain HTTPS beacon patterns.

tools.name: Covenant
tools.desc: Collaborative .NET C2 with a browser UI whose Grunt implants are dynamically compiled C# — the canonical worked example of .NET post-exploitation patterns (in-memory loading, AMSI/ETW patching, SMB P2P). Effectively unmaintained since ~2021 (last push 2024); now a lab/museum reference and signature-rich detection target.
tools.when: Studying .NET post-exploitation design and beating on well-known signatures in the lab; treat it as a legacy framework, not for live operations.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/cobbr/Covenant && cd Covenant/Covenant && dotnet build -c Release

tools.name: Villain
tools.desc: High-level stage 0/1 C2 handler for many reverse-TCP and HoaxShell (HTTPS) shells, shipped with Windows/Linux payload templates, fileless scripting, and cross-instance session sharing.
tools.when: Quick-sided Kali lab work that needs concurrent shell handling and payload-template experimentation without standing up a full framework.

tools.name: Cobalt Strike
tools.desc: Commercial threat-emulation platform (Fortra) and the de-facto reference C2; Malleable C2 profiles reshape HTTP(S)/DNS beacon traffic into the traffic shapes blue teams tune their detections around. Vetted licensing only: new licenses roughly $3.5k–$10k/user/yr, with cracked builds aggressively taken down.
tools.when: When you are an authorized red team that can buy it, or to study the beacon patterns that dominate C2 detection research.

tools.name: Brute Ratel C4
tools.desc: Commercial evasion-first C2 (Dark Vortex) built around the Badger implant and Commander UI, with EDR-bypass techniques (sleep obfuscation, hook removal) and a custom compiler introduced in v2.3 'Flux'. Single-user one-year license ~$3250; authorized owners only.
tools.when: Stress-testing EDR detections against an evasion-focused implant in your licensed lab; build a Brute Ratel detection story before it is needed in an incident.

tools.name: Nighthawk
tools.desc: Commercial C2 from MDSec's ActiveBreach team engineered for high-assurance detection evasion, with per-build watermarking (builds are attributable) and online-activated, hardware-locked licensing. ~$10k/user/yr, minimum three seats, UK export-controlled and vendor-vetted.
tools.when: Budgeted, mature red teams that can meet its vetting and seat minimum; otherwise, its published tradecraft makes a documented benchmark for hardening detector coverage.

tools.name: CrossC2
tools.desc: Extension that generates cross-platform beacons for Cobalt Strike (Linux, macOS, Android/ARM, even ESXi) from a configured HTTPS listener, via genCrossC2 plus automatic Malleable C2 profile handling.
tools.when: Extending a Cobalt Strike lab to authorized non-Windows assets where stock Beacon cannot run, or studying cross-platform beacon metadata.
tools.install: Download genCrossC2 + CrossC2.cna from the GitHub release

tools.name: Donut
tools.desc: Generates position-independent shellcode that stages .NET assemblies, PE files, and VBS/JScript entirely in memory, so a lab agent can be delivered without touching disk on the test host.
tools.when: Producing an in-memory delivery stage for a lab agent and observing how loaders that patch AMSI/ETW look from a defender's perspective.

tools.name: Ligolo-ng
tools.desc: Tunneling/pivoting tool that exposes a TUN interface and routes TCP/UDP through an agent over reverse TCP/TLS, reaching remote lab subnets without SOCKS/proxychains, with a web UI and autoroute since v0.8.
tools.when: Reaching the rest of an authorized test network from a C2 foothold — pivot activity blue teams should recognize and alert on.
tools.install: Download proxy & agent binaries from GitHub releases

tools.name: Chisel
tools.desc: Single-binary fast TCP/UDP tunnel carried over HTTP(S)/WebSocket (SSH-secured) with reverse port-forwarding and SOCKS — communication that reads as ordinary WebSocket/web traffic to defenders.
tools.when: Bridging egress-filtered lab segments to your C2, or tunnelling any service where the traffic should blend with normal HTTPS.
